terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to read today's order form.

tasks.title: Turn the quantity into a number
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/missing.js`, make a `const` called `quantity`: `quantityText` turned into a number. Print it.

Check runs your file with other quantities, one with spaces around the digits, and expects a number, not text that looks like one.
nextSteps: Run the file and read the second line: text plus one is not what Theo wants.
Find how the lesson turns text into a number.
Print it, and print `typeof quantity` too if you want to be sure.
hints: `'3'` with quotes is text. It looks like a number, but `+` joins it instead of adding.
JavaScript has a built-in that takes a value in its brackets and gives back the number it stands for.
The line has the shape `const quantity = Number(...)`, with `quantityText` in the brackets.

tasks.title: Give the note a default
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, make a `const` called `note`: `giftNote` when there is one, and the text `No note` when `giftNote` is `null` or `undefined`. A note that is empty text stays as it is. Print it.

Check tries `null`, `undefined`, a real note and an empty note.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on defaults.
Decide which of the two default operators fits: one replaces every falsy value, one only `null` and `undefined`.
Make `note` from `giftNote` and the default text.
Print it, then try a note at the top and run it again.
hints: You need a value that steps in only when nothing is there at all.
`||` would also replace empty text, because empty text is falsy. The task says empty text stays.
The line has the shape `const note = giftNote ?? '...'`, with the default text from the task in the quotes.

tasks.title: Spot text that is not a number
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make a `const` called `extraIsNumber`: `true` when `extraCandlesText` turns into a real number, `false` when it turns into `NaN`. Print it.

Check tries a word, digits, digits with a word after them, and more digits. It expects `true` or `false` itself.
nextSteps: Turn `extraCandlesText` into a number and print it to see what you get.
Find how the lesson asks whether a value is `NaN`.
Turn that answer around: you want true for a real number.
Print `extraIsNumber` and try other text at the top.
hints: First turn the text into a number. Bad text gives `NaN`.
`NaN === NaN` is false, so you cannot compare with it. `Number.isNaN(...)` asks the question for you.
`Number.isNaN(Number(extraCandlesText))` is true for bad text. Put `!` in front to flip it.

tasks.title: Fall back to one candle
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make a `const` called `safeQuantity`: `quantity` when it is a real number other than `0`, and `1` when it is `NaN` or `0`. Print it.

Check runs your file with a good quantity, a word, `'0'` and an empty box (`null`) in `quantityText`.
nextSteps: Make sure Task 1 passes: this task builds on `quantity`.
List what should become 1: `NaN` and `0`. Both are falsy.
Pick the default operator that replaces every falsy value.
Print it and try `'three'` at the top.
hints: Both values that should become 1 are falsy, and every good quantity is truthy.
This time you want the default operator that steps in for every falsy value, not only for `null` and `undefined`.
The line has the shape `const safeQuantity = quantity || ...`, with the fallback number in place of the dots.
